GPU-accelerated ray casting is a direct volume rendering method that offloads ray traversal and compositing to a graphics processing unit (GPU) to achieve real-time frame rates [S2].

The claim states that GPU-accelerated ray casting is a direct volume rendering method that offloads ray traversal and compositing to the GPU to achieve real-time frame rates. The evidence [S2] explicitly describes a GPU algorithm for ray casting (a form of direct volume rendering) where resampling and compositing are performed on the shader (GPU). It highlights that the GPU algorithm is significantly faster than the CPU, achieving an average time of ~15ms compared to ~9486ms for the CPU, which proves 'much stronger real-time efficiency' and meets 'real-time requirement of interactive.' The evidence supports the mechanism (offloading to GPU/shader) and the outcome (real-time performance).
supported
